newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to offer electronic tickets.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to offer electronic tickets.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Thursday it plans to introduce international ticketless air travel in mid-1997.

Anselm Egger, manager of Lufthansa's electronic ticketing, told a meeting of travel agents that he expected Lufthansa to start full electronic ticketing outside Germany on routes to North America in cooperation with United Airlines.
He said the offering would be made after the International Association of Travel Agents (IATA) agrees to ticket standards.
Lufthansa would then extend ticketless travel to interline agreements with other airlines, Egger said.
Egger told Reuters the airline decided to start electronic ticketing outside Germany on services to Paris and London since these were the most profitable business travel routes.
He said check-in machines would be installed at London Heathrow and Paris' Charles de Gaulle airport.

In addition, he said that from November 1 all members of Lufthansa's frequent flier programme with a credit card will be able to book all inner-German flights by telephone and receive boarding passes from airport check-in machines.
The chip card/smart card to be issued to frequent fliers will gain additional functions such as telephone, credit card and hotel card functions.
